title: Worked-example projects read the greeting string from a fixed config path
context: The worked-example library exists to make external-library authoring concrete for readers of docs/library-authoring.md. It ships one blueprint whose whole surface is a greeting string; that blueprint needs one project-level decision it can land, so the doc has an ADR to point at when explaining how library ADRs stamp with a suffix under the library prefix (ADR-6001-wla-example-standard, inside the library's declared adr suffix block 6000..6099).
decision: Projects that apply the wla:example-standard blueprint read the greeting string from a single config key, exampleGreetingPath, at project start. The default value is 'config/greeting.txt' relative to the project root; projects that want a different path override the key in their runtime config. No other side effects; no dependencies.
consequences: The library contributes exactly one REQ and one ADR, both stamped under the wla prefix. A project applying wla:example-standard will see the ADR appear at rcf/adrs/adr-6001-wla-example-standard.json and the REQ at rcf/requirements/wla-example-standard-req-60001.json. Removing the library refuses on the applied REQ per phase-1 library-ownership semantics until the operator drops the blueprint from the project.
